Kinchkha Waterfall

A cascade waterfall roughly a hundred metres high above Okatse, at the end of a gravel road.

Time needed
2 h
From Tbilisi
275 km · 4:15
Road
Unpaved sections
Car needed
Crossover / SUV
Season
May–October
Entry
~15 ₾ + შატლი ~5 ₾

Kinchkha Waterfall lies above Okatse Canyon in Khoni municipality, and both belong to the same protected area. The water drops down a limestone wall in several stages; the total height reaches around a hundred metres, but it is a cascade rather than a single fall.

Seasonality defines the visit more than anything else. In spring and after heavy rain the waterfall is loud and powerful; by late August it often shrinks to a thin ribbon. If you want the dramatic version, May and June are the right months.

Getting there is its own story. The final stretch is gravel with deep ruts and becomes considerably harder after rain. For that reason a shuttle from the visitor centre is usually offered, and driving your own car all the way up is not always recommended. From the parking area, wooden stairs and a path lead down to the viewing decks.

What you get:

  • views of the falls from two levels
  • Colchic forest gorge and limestone walls
  • the option of combining it with Okatse Canyon in one day

Both sites fit into a single day, but only if you leave Tbilisi early. Attempting Kinchkha as an afternoon add-on after a late start regularly ends with people arriving as the last shuttle leaves.

Practical advice

The falls are fullest in May and June and can shrink dramatically by the end of summer. The last section of road is gravel — if you are in a sedan, leave it at the visitor centre and take the shuttle up. The wooden stairs are slippery in rain, so shoes with grip are essential. Bring water and food, as there is no shop above. Toilets are only at the visitor centre, and the nearest ATM is in Khoni.

How to get there from Tbilisi

From Tbilisi take the E60 to Kutaisi, then head towards Khoni and Gordi — 275 km and roughly four hours fifteen. Beyond Gordi the road towards Kinchkha narrows, and the final five or six kilometres are gravel with steep pitches and washouts after rain. A sedan is a poor choice on that section; a crossover or the shuttle is much better. In winter the track is often impassable. Fill up in Kutaisi or Khoni.
